title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors, officers and employees
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of Champion Iron Limited and its subsidiaries. Subject to the general Dealing, Communication and Procurement Prohibitions on trading or tipping while in possession of Privileged or Price-Sensitive Information; the blackout periods, pre-clearance, anti-hedging, margin lending/secured financing and short-term dealing restrictions apply only to Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders.

tiers.name: Reporting Insiders
tiers.description: Any director of the Company, as well as any director, officer or employee of the Company or a subsidiary designated by the Company as a reporting insider within the meaning of Canadian National Instrument 55-104. Subject to blackout periods, pre-clearance, anti-hedging restrictions, margin lending/secured financing approval, short-term dealing/short-selling approval, and SEDI insider reporting.

tiers.name: Designated Insiders
tiers.description: A director, officer or employee of the Company or a subsidiary designated by the Company as subject to trading restrictions due to access to Privileged or Price-Sensitive Information, including KMP, and family members and closely connected persons of such people designated by the Company as being subject to certain trading restrictions. Subject to the same blackout period, pre-clearance, anti-hedging, margin lending/secured financing and short-term dealing restrictions as Reporting Insiders.

tiers.name: Executive Chairman
tiers.description: The Executive Chairman, a Reporting Insider distinguished only by approval routing: pre-clearance, margin lending/secured financing approval, and short-term dealing/short-selling approval route to the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Lead Director rather than to the Executive Chairman.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders shall not in respect of Company Securities engage in transactions in derivatives in respect of Company Securities (such as put and call options), or any other hedging or equity monetization transaction in which the individual's economic interest and risk exposure in Company Securities is changed (such as collars or forward sales contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an outright, unconditional ban on the exact structure proposed — a collar is named verbatim — with no exceptional-circumstances or approval route available anywhere in the policy, unlike blackout-period trading, margin lending or short-term dealing, each of which can be approved.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders must not engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities without prior approval of the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan secured on the collared shares could in principle be approved, but this approval cannot cure the absolute ban on the derivative legs, so the funded collar as a package cannot proceed even though its financing component is only conditionally restricted.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman may provide written clearance to a Reporting Insider or Designated Insider to trade in Company Securities during a regular blackout period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This waiver mechanism is expressly limited to trading during a blackout period; it has no application to the Anti-Hedging Restrictions, confirming there is no back door for a collar even in hardship or court-ordered circumstances.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any other instrument, agreement or understanding that affects, directly or indirectly, a person's economic interest in a security of the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The definition is broad enough to capture almost any synthetic or economic-exposure structure, reinforcing that a funded collar cannot be engineered around the express derivatives/hedging ban by re-labelling it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the Executive Chairman wishes to engage in any margin lending or other secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, he must first submit a pre-clearing request to the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Lead Director.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collar's loan leg were sought by the Executive Chairman specifically, approval routes to the Lead Director instead of the Executive Chairman approving himself.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Reporting Insiders or Designated Insiders (directors, KMP, and other designated officers/employees, together with their designated family members and closely connected persons) under this policy. The Anti-Hedging Restrictions impose an absolute, unconditional ban on 'transactions in derivatives in respect of Company Securities (such as put and call options), or any other hedging or equity monetization transaction ... (such as collars or forward sales contracts)' — collars are named verbatim — and unlike every other restriction in the policy (blackout-period trading, margin lending, short-term dealing/short selling), there is no approval, pre-clearance or exceptional-circumstances route that can lift it. The loan leg is only conditionally restricted: a margin loan or other secured financing arrangement over Company Securities requires prior approval of the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary and the Executive Chairman (or, for the Executive Chairman himself, the Lead Director), but this approval cannot cure the absolute ban on the derivative legs. Reporting Insiders and Designated Insiders may otherwise trade only within the open window beginning the third business day after quarterly, half-yearly or annual results and ending at the close of the following financial quarter, subject to written pre-clearance valid for five trading days and any discretionary blackout period imposed by the General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. Directors, officers and employees outside these two tiers face only the general insider trading prohibition, but they are also the population unlikely to hold the vested incentive equity a collar would be written over.
